Which of the following is the correct nodal admittance matrix \( Y_B \)?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is node/bus U1, and the right side is node/bus U2; the upper and lower two parallel branches respectively connect U1 and U2 through transformers T1 and T2. Reasoning: According to the problem statement and the specified method, the equivalent impedance of each transformer is j0.1 p.u., so the branch admittance y = 1/(j0.1) = -j10. T1 has the rated transformation ratio, take a1 = 1, and its nodal admittance matrix is Y_T1 = y[[1,-1],[-1,1]] = [[-j10, j10],[j10, -j10]]. The high-voltage-side tap of T2 is +5%, take a2 = 1.05; according to the high-voltage-side tap model, Y_T2 = y[[1,-1/1.05],[-1/1.05,1/(1.05)^2]]. Therefore the corresponding terms of T2 are Y11 = -j10, Y12 = Y21 = j10/1.05 = j9.5238, Y22 = -j10/(1.05)^2 = -j9.0703. The two transformers are connected in parallel, and the nodal admittance matrices are added: Y11 = -j10 + (-j10) = -j20; Y12 = Y21 = j10 + j9.5238 = j19.524; Y22 = -j10 + (-j9.0703) = -j19.07.

method.method_draft: Describe the figure as two transformer branches T1 and T2 in parallel between buses U1 and U2, with the load at the U2 side. Given \(\dot{U}_2 = 1 \angle 0^{\circ}\), transformer \(\mathrm{T}_1\) is at the rated turns ratio, transformer \(\mathrm{T}_2\) has a high-side tap setting of \(+5\%\), and the impedance referred to the primary side is \(\mathrm{j}0.1\) per unit, what is the nodal admittance matrix \(Y_B\)?

Image description: In the figure, the left side is node/bus U1, and the right side is node/bus U2; the upper and lower two parallel branches respectively connect U1 and U2 through transformers T1 and T2. The U2 bus on the right side also has a load arrow pointing to the right, indicating that two step-up transformers are connected in parallel to supply power to the load.
Reasoning: According to the problem statement and the specified method, the equivalent impedance of each transformer is j0.1 p.u., so the branch admittance y = 1/(j0.1) = -j10. T1 has the rated transformation ratio, take a1 = 1, and its nodal admittance matrix is Y_T1 = y[[1,-1],[-1,1]] = [[-j10, j10],[j10, -j10]]. The high-voltage-side tap of T2 is +5%, take a2 = 1.05; according to the high-voltage-side tap model, Y_T2 = y[[1,-1/1.05],[-1/1.05,1/(1.05)^2]]. Therefore the corresponding terms of T2 are Y11 = -j10, Y12 = Y21 = j10/1.05 = j9.5238, Y22 = -j10/(1.05)^2 = -j9.0703. The two transformers are connected in parallel, and the nodal admittance matrices are added: Y11 = -j10 + (-j10) = -j20; Y12 = Y21 = j10 + j9.5238 = j19.524; Y22 = -j10 + (-j9.0703) = -j19.07.
